title: Interactive continental explorer defaults
interpretation: Population values are coarse regional teaching presets. Migration and mixing values are modeler-chosen sensitivity defaults, not measured historical rates.

population_preset_9000_bce.status: secondary-source regional reconstruction; values rounded to people

aggregation_notes.Asia: Asia 1,317,000 + CIS 238,000 in the source table
aggregation_notes.Americas: Latin America 363,000 + North America 52,000 in the source table

source.label: Statista historical continental population table, 9000 BCE row
source.note: Used because the table provides a separate Middle East category. Prehistoric values are highly uncertain.

population_target_2000_ce.status: same source-compatible endpoint; used only to create a smooth visual population trajectory

global_crosscheck.finding: Global population estimate for 10,000 BCE about 4.4 million, with very wide uncertainty (<0.01 to 8.9 million in the paper's scenario range).

parent_source_offdiag_default.status: modeler-chosen teaching sensitivity preset; NOT an empirical Holocene migration matrix
parent_source_offdiag_default.semantics: row=destination child's region, column=source region; value=fraction of parental draws from that external region per generation

mixing_strength_default.status: modeler-chosen sensitivity parameter; 0=no descendant-status diffusion beyond pooled composition, 1=full random mating within macroregion

late_contact_default.status: teaching sensitivity control, not an empirical global contact estimate

population_anchors_bce.status: secondary-source regional reconstruction used for date-responsive teaching presets; values are people
population_anchors_bce.interpolation: Notebook log-interpolates between adjacent 1000-year anchors. This interpolation is a modeling convenience, not additional historical evidence.

source.label: Statista historical continental population table, 9000 BCE row
source.note: Used because the table provides a separate Middle East category. Prehistoric values are highly uncertain.
